description: The one source of the architecture/dependency rule (AGENTS 28, master backlog P0 #2). Read by tools/architecture/check-dependencies.mjs (the tool that fails a build) and by tests/architecture/dependencies.test.ts (the suite that keeps the tool honest). Nothing else may restate these edges — a second copy is a second rule.

@vdp/charts.why: DOM-free chart core; knows its own types and nothing else.

@vdp/protocols-oem.why: Manufacturer hook types and registry; fills gaps, depends on nothing.

@vdp/domain.why: Domain contracts: shared primitives only — never protocols, transports or I/O.

@vdp/application.why: Application layer: commands/queries/actions speak domain only.

@vdp/definitions.why: Definitions are data + validation; no diagnostic logic.

@vdp/transport-doip.why: DoIP presents itself as a CAN-like link; it never pulls in the protocol layer.

@vdp/protocols-uds.why: Speaks through a link interface, never through a bus or adapter.

@vdp/protocols-kwp2000.why: Legacy ECUs share the UDS primitives.

@vdp/adapter-generic-can.why: Adapter implements the bus contract; hardware specifics stay here.

@vdp/adapter-elm327.why: Serial ELM327 protocol and stream belong to the adapter.

@vdp/adapter-host.why: Host bindings (tty, bindings loader) and the side-effect-free probe catalog.

@vdp/core.why: The diagnostic core: protocols + transports + definitions (still the widest package below runtime).

@vdp/runtime.why: Composition root: wires the transport seam, so it may reach the concrete transports while domain/application stay free of them.

@vdp/storage.why: Persistence and export formats below the runtime.

@vdp/reports.why: Report rendering prints what the core produced.

@vdp/ai.why: Provider abstraction stays orthogonal to diagnostics.

@vdp/simulators.why: Virtual vehicle answers like a real ECU stack.

@vdp/trace-analyzer.why: Offline trace tooling decodes with the protocol layer, without the core.

@vdp/definition-importer.why: Imports definition data; validation is the definitions package.

@vdp/web.why: The workbench speaks to the vehicle exclusively through the runtime (command/query bus).

nodeBuiltins.why: Portable layers (domain, application, protocols, transports, core, runtime) must stay free of node:fs and sockets; file system and host bindings belong to storage, host adapters and apps.

ui.why: No package imports the UI — the app depends on the layers, never the other way round.

layerRules.why: Protocols speak through a link, never through an adapter.
Transports are the frame layer; protocols sit above them.
Hardware specifics stay below protocols and the core.

portableLayers.why: Domain and application stay protocol-, transport- and I/O-free (AGENTS 1, 3).
